items.followUp: How does shielding effect change down a group and across a period?

rubric.why: The answer states the increase in shielding effect down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding effect increases down a group, because additional electron shells provide more shielding and make the inner electrons less affected by the nucleus.

rubric.why: The answer describes the usual textbook trend across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding effect remains almost constant across a period.

modelAnswer: Shielding effect increases down a group because new electron shells are added.
Across a period, shielding effect remains almost constant.

items.followUp: Why do elements of groups 13 and 14 belong to the p-block?

rubric.why: The answer identifies the subshell receiving the last or valence electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the last (or valence) electron enters an s-subshell.

rubric.why: The answer gives the number of outer s-electrons for groups 1 and 2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that group 1 elements have one and group 2 elements have two electrons in the outer s-subshell.

modelAnswer: Groups 1 and 2 are called the s-block because their last electron enters an s-subshell.
Group 1 elements have one outer s-electron, while group 2 elements have two.

items.followUp: Name four common types of chemical bonds.

rubric.why: The answer names two of the four required bond types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ionic (or electrovalent) and covalent bonds.

rubric.why: The answer names the other two bond types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming coordinate covalent (or dative) and metallic bonds.

modelAnswer: The four types are ionic, covalent, coordinate covalent and metallic bonds.

items.followUp: In a coordinate covalent bond, what does the acceptor provide, and what does the donor provide?

rubric.why: The answer identifies the electron pair supplied by the donor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the donor atom or ion provides both electrons of the shared pair (a lone pair).

rubric.why: The answer identifies the role or available orbital of the acceptor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the acceptor receives the donated pair, usually into a vacant orbital.

modelAnswer: The donor provides both electrons of the shared pair as a lone pair.
The acceptor receives this pair and usually has a vacant orbital to accommodate it.

items.followUp: How does an electronegativity difference cause a polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: The answer explains that the bonding electrons are not shared equally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a polar covalent bond forms when bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally, typically because they have different electronegativities.

rubric.why: The answer states the resulting separation of charge in the bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative ends (poles).

modelAnswer: A polar covalent bond forms when bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally because of a difference in electronegativity.
This unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative ends in the bond.

items.followUp: How do weak intermolecular forces affect the rate of evaporation?

rubric.why: The answer identifies intermolecular forces as affecting how readily molecules escape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that intermolecular forces hold liquid molecules together and influence their escape from the surface.

rubric.why: The answer gives the correct relationship between force strength and evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stronger intermolecular forces slow evaporation, while weaker forces make evaporation faster.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces hold liquid molecules together and affect how easily they escape from the surface.
Stronger intermolecular forces slow evaporation; weaker forces make evaporation faster.

items.followUp: What happens to the vapour pressure of a liquid when its temperature is lowered? Explain briefly.

rubric.why: The answer gives the correct direction of change as temperature rises.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vapour pressure increases when the temperature increases.

rubric.why: The answer explains the increase in vapour pressure through greater molecular motion or evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that molecules gain kinetic energy, so more escape into the vapour phase.

modelAnswer: When the temperature of a liquid increases, its vapour pressure increases.
The molecules gain kinetic energy, so more of them escape into the vapour phase.

items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and an unsaturated solution.

rubric.why: The answer gives the defining solute limit for a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature, so no more solute can dissolve.

rubric.why: The answer states that an unsaturated solution can still dissolve additional solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an unsaturated solution contains less than the maximum amount of solute and can dissolve more at that temperature.

modelAnswer: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature; no more solute can dissolve.
An unsaturated solution contains less than this maximum amount and can dissolve more solute at that temperature.
